title: Terrorblade Aqirs

sources.label: ENDGAME Rank Up ALL ★★★ MEGA Build For Dota Auto Chess

body:
# Terrorblade Aqirs

This build is built around a single item-hungry carry rather than a wide
synergy board: a 3-star Terrorblade that periodically transforms a nearby
ally into a demon illusion copy of itself. Those illusions inherit useful
traits from whichever unit they were made from — an Assassin's crit chance,
a Satyr's fear, a stun already cast — and every item sitting on the main
Terrorblade is copied onto them too, so the whole plan is to stack two or
three exceptional items on Terrorblade and let the clones multiply that
value across the board. It's less consistent early than a synergy-first
build (Terrorblade is mediocre at 1-2★ and does very little until items
come online), but a fully itemized 3-star Terrorblade is one of the hardest
things in the game to answer, since it silences casters, fears the front
line, crits like an Assassin, and eventually deals a portion of its damage
as unmitigated pure damage.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Terrorblade | 3 | Demon, Demon Hunter | Main carry — 3-star priority #1, transforms adjacent allies into itemized illusions |
| Riki | 3 | Assassin, Satyr | Best transform target — illusion keeps Assassin crit and can silence casters when Riki himself is 3★ |
| Spirit Breaker | 1 | Assassin, Tauren | Second-best transform target — cheap, and a 3★ Spirit Breaker gives its illusion form a much higher base damage |
| Sand King | 3 | Aqir, Assassin | Positioned to cast its stun first, then get pulled into the transform so the illusion still benefits from the stun having landed |
| Bane | 1 | Faceless, Satyr, Warlock | Frontline fear bait — cheap, disposable, softens the enemy front line before Terrorblade activates |
| Venomancer | 3 | Aqir, Beast, Warlock | Secondary Warlock body and a contributor toward the 2-Beast damage buff |

Fill remaining slots with two more Warlock-tagged units (Witch Doctor and
Lifestealer are the cheapest fits) to reach 4 Warlocks, plus one more
Beast-tagged unit (Monkey King is a reasonable pick) to activate the 2-Beast
bonus alongside Venomancer.

## Items

Itemization matters more than synergy count here — everything goes on
Terrorblade first, since illusions inherit it. Tier 1-2 items are only
useful as stepping stones: **Bottle** speeds up Terrorblade's cast time,
and **Sliver** is worth holding purely to combine toward a Tier 5. Tier 3
items (**Linkens Sphere**, **Moon Shard**) are fine placeholders but not
worth rerolling for specifically. Tier 4s worth grabbing along the way are
**Minotaur Horn** (guarantees Terrorblade can transform instantly instead of
whiffing a cast), **Manta Style**, **Butterfly**, and **Monkey King Bar**.

The actual power spike is two specific Tier 5 items: one offensive
(**Daedalus** or **Mjollnir**) paired with one defensive (**Aeon Disk**,
whose 100% damage block for 3.5 seconds when critically low is what makes a
3-star Terrorblade essentially unkillable in extended fights). Don't
craft down into random Tier 5s just to fill the slot — reroll a Tier 3/4
item instead if you don't have the pieces for one of these specifically; a
generic Tier 5 isn't worth losing the item identity that makes the build
function. The **Weaponsmith** relic (upgrades the loot tier you get from
recasting equipment) is a strong way to accelerate into a real Tier 5 if
you're short on gold to buy up naturally.

## Relics

Take any relic that boosts economy or improves your odds at Tier 5 items —
this build lives or dies by hitting a good Tier 5 on Terrorblade, and you
generally can't force one before round 25 without help. **Lucid Star**
(chance to instantly upgrade a purchased unit to 2-star) is excellent here
specifically because it can hand you a 2-star Terrorblade far ahead of
schedule — remember to disable auto-fuse while it's active so a lucky 2-star
proc doesn't get auto-combined away. Don't activate it the moment you find
it: you only get 10 rounds of uptime, so hold it until you actually have the
economy and roll-down plan ready to capitalize (round 15-16 is the video's
benchmark).

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Level 7 is the sweet spot to sit at for most of the game — it gives the
best odds at Tier 3 units (Terrorblade's cost) without diluting the pool
the way level 8 does. Take the **Greedy** talent at the first opportunity to
cut reroll costs, and hold off on heavy rolling until you have both the
gold and a saved relic ready, since a wasted roll-down with no relic backing
it is the build's biggest economy leak. Priority order for 3-stars is
Terrorblade first, then Riki, then a choice between Sand King and Spirit
Breaker (Spirit Breaker is the better pick specifically because 3-star base
stats carry over strongly into its illusion form), then Venomancer, with
Bane dead last — Bane's fear is useful even at 1-star and it's not worth
spending rolls chasing its third copy. Aim to have Terrorblade 3-starred by
round 26; missing that benchmark leaves you noticeably behind on
survivability against high-level lobbies. Around level 8-9, pick up the
second Beast piece and the third/fourth Warlock pieces respectively — the
4-Warlock 20% team-wide lifesteal is what turns Terrorblade's damage into
real sustain.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Place Spirit Breaker and Riki directly adjacent to Terrorblade so they're
prioritized as transform targets, and keep Bane on the front line to fear
incoming attackers before the rest of the plan comes online. Sand King
should sit where it will cast its stun into the enemy team before drifting
back toward Terrorblade to be transformed after the stun has already gone
off. A 3-star Riki (transformed or not) should be positioned to cover
whichever half of the enemy board is stacked with mana-hungry casters — its
silence-on-engage shuts down instant-cast mage lineups (Dragon Mage in
particular) before they can burst you down.

This build is strong specifically because a fully itemized Terrorblade
answers almost everything: it fears, silences, crits, and deals partial
pure damage, so it doesn't have one obvious counter-comp the way a pure
synergy board does. The two real threats are direct anti-carry tools —
Hex-type disables that stop Terrorblade from transforming shut the whole
plan down, since the build's entire value is tied up in one unit — and
simply running out the clock without a Tier 5 item, since a bare 3-star
Terrorblade without itemization is little more than an average duelist.
